result.recommendation: Read `dab."v_<SRC>_<NAME>_<TGT>"` filtered on `rel_name` and `row_st = 'Y'`; deduplicate it with `row_number()` partitioned by the source key, ordered by `eff_tmstp DESC, ver_tmstp DESC` and then the target key so the pick is reproducible; resolve it as of the **end** of the stage version's validity, which on a transaction stage is open and therefore means the latest pair; and LEFT JOIN it into the stage CTE so an order whose customer is unknown keeps its row and inherits a null key. The direction of the walk is the declared `source_entity_id -> target_entity_id`, with no cardinality declared anywhere, because the mapping grammar can only express one target per source row and §1.2 already forces the name to read as a sentence in that direction; a generated data check pins the half the grammar cannot cover. The walk is one hop and unbounded in breadth; a second hop is a refusal with a fixture that tests it. `entity_keys()` and the peripheral set are redefined as every entity the declarations touch **or reach**, so a reached entity with no event of its own still gets a key column and a peripheral table.

consequences.text: An order with no customer keeps its row and its freight, and the null key groups as itself. Measured on the probe: the orphan CH6 contributes 60.00 of a 210.75 total, and it is the null group that carries it. An INNER JOIN loses it silently; nothing in the recording would have shown that today.

The bridge cannot multiply a measure by relationship history, because the key read emits one row per source key by construction rather than by trust. The declaration decides which key is inherited; the SQL decides that exactly one arrives.

The as-of rule is written in `dar/uss/_bridge.sql`, so a reader can see when the inherited key was true without reading a vendor macro whose default parameter is not even visible in `duckdb_functions()`.

Filtering on `rel_name` makes a second edge between the same two entities a new structure rather than a silent collision, and never depends on `type_key`, which is a deploy-time surrogate that differed between two probes of the same shape.
One pair CTE per edge rather than per (stage, edge), because the resolution does not depend on the stage row. With three stages walking one edge the generated SQL grows by one CTE, not three.

Defining the key columns and the peripherals by the walk's reach means `customer_key` and `dar__uss.customer` exist for an entity that has no event, which is the only reason the question can be answered.

The model cannot say that an edge is *not* many-to-one, so a many-to-many relationship would be walked and would attribute a measure to an arbitrary one of its targets. The total stays right, the breakdown does not, and nothing prevents it before the build — `adss build` does not run `adss check`, so the warehouse exists and a page can render before the check reports it.

A tie is resolved by alphabetical order on the target key. That is stable and reproducible and it is not a business rule. It is defensible only because a check refuses to let a tie through unremarked; if the check is ever weakened, one row's country is decided by the alphabet.

Slice 2's own acceptance query cannot tell a correct implementation from one that never reads the relationship. All 830 orders in the recording ship to their own customer's country, so grouping by `order.destination_country` yields byte-identical output. The reconciliation that gives every other slice its confidence is blind to this one.

`v_<SRC>_<NAME>_<TGT>` is an engine-internal view with no compatibility promise, on a platform the vendor does not list as supported. This adds a fourth engine behaviour the generated layer depends on, and the only thing that turns a vendor change into a failure rather than a null column is a pinning check.
The walk stops at one hop, so slice 5 cannot build until it is generalised. That is deliberate and it arrives as a refusal, but it does mean a slice will open on a build that will not run.

Adding an entity inserts a key column between the last key and the first measure, so every measure's ordinal position shifts even though no name changes. Consumers are written against names and §1.3 forbids `SELECT *`, so the exposure is confined to the union's own branches — which is exactly why ADR 0002's branch-order test matters more now than it did with one branch.

A foreign key set to null is never retracted: re-landing an order with no customer writes no pair row, no tombstone and no `row_st` flip, so the stale customer survives forever. The probe reproduced it (CH2 kept P2 after its parent code went null). This is the engine's behaviour, not a consequence of the choice, but it is the choice that will be blamed for it.

result.confirmation:
Four things, and the first is the one that carries the weight, because the question's own reconciliation cannot.

**A machinery test over a neutral fixture, executing the generated bridge.** `tests/fixtures/dab/` already holds PARENT, CHILD and NEIGHBOUR with two edges from CHILD, one of them to an entity with no event. The test builds `dab."view_<E>_hist"` and `dab."v_<SRC>_<NAME>_<TGT>"` as in-memory tables from data files, runs `bridge_sql` over them, and asserts three things at once: the sum equals the fixture total, the orphan's row survives with a null inherited key, and a source key with two pair versions produces exactly one row. This is the pattern `tests/test_das_executes.py` already uses (an in-memory warehouse built from a contract fixture), so it is not new machinery, and no business word appears in it. I ran this shape by hand against a real deployed DAB and it returns 6 rows, 210.75, CH6 with a null key, and by-parent totals P1 90.00 / P2 30.75 / P3 30.00 / null 60.00.

**Structural machinery tests**: that `bridge_columns` includes a key column for an entity that is only *reached* and never evented; that the generated SQL joins `LEFT` and ranks with `row_number()` rather than `rank()`; and that a `bad_two_hop_walk.yaml` fixture is refused with a message naming what slice 5 must decide, so the deferral is tested rather than remembered.

**Three generated data checks**, all of which I ran against the real engine and which behaved exactly as designed — `0`, `1`, `0` on a probe with one deliberate ambiguity:

1. *Conservation*: distinct source keys in `view_<E>_hist` whose event date is set, minus the stage's row count, must be zero. This is the single check that catches every failure in this record — the INNER JOIN drops rows and it goes negative, the undeduplicated pair join multiplies and it goes positive, a tie multiplies and it goes positive.
2. *Tie-freedom*: rank the pairs with `rank()` (so ties survive) and assert `count(*) - count(DISTINCT source_key) = 0`. Same shape as the existing `checks/orders__key.sql`.
3. *Strangers*: no bridge row carries a non-null inherited key that is not a pair the business layer actually recorded — which is the shape a misspelled M6 target expression takes, since the engine reports nothing at deploy or at execute and the column is simply null.

**The existing gates, widened.** `adss dar generate --check` fails on any diff. The `view_<E>_with_rel` pin must be rewritten before it can pass: it currently asserts of *every* entity that `_with_rel` equals the plain view, which is true only on a relationship's source side and fails the moment CUSTOMER becomes a target. Every statement above lints clean under the repository's own `.sqlfluff` — I ran `sqlfluff lint` on the bridge, the peripheral, both question queries and all three checks, and all returned "All Finished!" with no violations.

What this does **not** confirm is the fan-out property D-0001 rests on. ORDER and CUSTOMER are the same grain and CUSTOMER owns no measure, so no measure can multiply across the edge however the join is written. What slice 2 does newly demonstrate is multiplication from the relationship's *own history*, which is a real fan trap and was not anticipated. The deviations register should record D-0001 as half discharged, with the cross-grain half still waiting for slice 4.
result.concreteShape:
## 1. `dab/uss.yaml` — the literal file for slice 2

The structural point is the negative space: no relationship block appears here, and the header says why, because a reader's first question on seeing a key inherit is "where is that declared?".

```yaml
# What the generated star schema needs to know that the business model does not otherwise
# say: which date makes an entity a measurement event, and which numbers are its measures.
#
# These are business facts -- "an order is placed on a day, and counting orders means
# counting orders" -- so every one carries its own definition. The glossary copies these
# strings; it never composes one. Names follow docs/conventions.md section 2.
#
# There is deliberately no relationships block. A relationship is declared once, in
# model.yaml, and the generator walks it from source to target because that is the only
# direction a mapping can express: a target_transformation_expression reads one row of a
# table keyed by the source entity (M5), so a source row names at most one target. The
# cardinality is therefore not restated here; it is pinned by a generated data check. ADR 0006.
uss:
  events:
    - id: PLACED
      entity: ORDER
      definition: >-
        An order was placed: the business accepted a customer's request and committed to
        supplying it. One per order, on the day it was accepted.
      kind: transaction
      date_attribute: PLACED_ON
      measures:
        - id: PLACED_ORDERS_COUNT
          definition: >-
            The number of orders placed. One for each order, counted on the day the business
            accepted it, regardless of what was on it or whether it was ever delivered.
          aggregate: count

        - id: FREIGHT_ORDERS_AMOUNT
          definition: >-
            What the business paid to have placed orders carried, attributed to the day it
            accepted each one. It is a cost of fulfilment, so it is additive over any set of
            orders and over any period -- but only over orders, since one order carries one
            freight charge however many items are on it.
          aggregate: sum
          attribute: FREIGHT_CHARGE
```

## 2. `dar/uss/_bridge.sql` — the literal generated bridge

Slice 2 has **one** stage. A second stage would need a second `(entity, event)` pair, and CUSTOMER has no date attribute in the model; a `kind: snapshot` event is refused by `read_uss` today and ADR 0002 defers it. Inventing one to get a second branch would be inventing an event to obtain a table. Lints clean under `.sqlfluff`.

```sql
-- Generated from dab/model.yaml and dab/uss.yaml. Do not edit; regenerate.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE dar__uss._bridge AS
WITH pair__order_is_placed_by_customer AS (
    SELECT
        edge."ORDER_key" AS order_key,
        edge."CUSTOMER_key" AS customer_key
    FROM dab."v_ORDER_IS_PLACED_BY_CUSTOMER" AS edge
    WHERE edge.rel_name = 'ORDER_IS_PLACED_BY_CUSTOMER' AND edge.row_st = 'Y'
    QUALIFY row_number() OVER (
        PARTITION BY edge."ORDER_key"
        ORDER BY edge.eff_tmstp DESC, edge.ver_tmstp DESC, edge."CUSTOMER_key" ASC
    ) = 1
),

placed AS (
    SELECT
        placed."ORDER_key" AS order_key,
        pair_customer.customer_key AS customer_key,
        placed.eff_tmstp AS _observed_at,
        cast(placed."PLACED_ON" AS DATE) AS _event_date,
        cast(1 AS BIGINT) AS _measure__order__placed_orders_count,
        cast(placed."FREIGHT_CHARGE" AS DECIMAL(28, 8)) AS _measure__order__freight_orders_amount
    FROM dab."view_ORDER_hist" AS placed
    LEFT JOIN pair__order_is_placed_by_customer AS pair_customer
        ON placed."ORDER_key" = pair_customer.order_key
    WHERE placed."PLACED_ON" IS NOT NULL
    QUALIFY row_number() OVER (
        PARTITION BY placed."ORDER_key"
        ORDER BY placed.eff_tmstp DESC
    ) = 1
)

SELECT
    'order' AS _stage,
    'placed' AS _event,
    placed._event_date AS _event_date,
    TRUE AS _is_current,
    placed._observed_at AS _observed_at,
    placed.order_key AS order_key,
    placed.customer_key AS customer_key,
    placed._measure__order__placed_orders_count AS _measure__order__placed_orders_count,
    placed._measure__order__freight_orders_amount AS _measure__order__freight_orders_amount
FROM placed AS placed;
```

Column contract, in order: `_stage, _event, _event_date, _is_current, _observed_at, order_key, customer_key, _measure__order__placed_orders_count, _measure__order__freight_orders_amount`.

**What a second stage adds**, so the discipline is legible before slice 4 needs it. A stage on an entity with no outgoing walked edge emits `cast(NULL AS VARCHAR) AS customer_key`; every branch emits a typed `NULL` for every measure it does not own; a stage that walks the same edge reuses the one `pair__…` CTE above rather than emitting its own:

```sql
UNION ALL

SELECT
    'customer' AS _stage,
    'observed' AS _event,
    observed._event_date AS _event_date,
    observed._is_current AS _is_current,
    observed._observed_at AS _observed_at,
    cast(NULL AS VARCHAR) AS order_key,
    observed.customer_key AS customer_key,
    cast(NULL AS BIGINT) AS _measure__order__placed_orders_count,
    cast(NULL AS DECIMAL(28, 8)) AS _measure__order__freight_orders_amount
FROM observed AS observed
```

## 3. `dar/uss/customer.sql` — the peripheral the walk's reach creates

CUSTOMER has no event, so under slice 1's rule this file would not exist. It exists because the walk reaches CUSTOMER.

```sql
-- Generated from dab/model.yaml and dab/uss.yaml. Do not edit; regenerate.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE dar__uss.customer AS
SELECT
    e."CUSTOMER_key" AS customer_key,
    e.eff_tmstp AS _observed_at,
    e."CUSTOMER_CODE" AS customer_code,
    e."TRADING_NAME" AS trading_name,
    e."BASED_IN_COUNTRY" AS based_in_country
FROM dab."view_CUSTOMER_hist" AS e
QUALIFY row_number() OVER (
    PARTITION BY e."CUSTOMER_key"
    ORDER BY e.eff_tmstp DESC
) = 1;
```

## 4. `docs/questions/02-…/uss.sql` — the answer

`INNER` on the calendar and on the row's own stage key; `LEFT` on the **inherited** key, which is ADR 0002's query-time rule and the reason an order with no customer still contributes its freight, to a null country group.

```sql
-- The answer, from the generated star schema. This is what the destination reads.
SELECT
    cal.quarter_label AS order_quarter,
    c.based_in_country AS customer_country,
    cast(sum(b._measure__order__freight_orders_amount) AS DECIMAL(28, 8)) AS freight_orders_amount
FROM dar__uss._bridge AS b
INNER JOIN dar__uss._calendar AS cal ON b._event_date = cal.date_key
LEFT JOIN dar__uss.customer AS c ON b.customer_key = c.customer_key
WHERE b._event = 'placed'
GROUP BY cal.quarter_label, c.based_in_country
ORDER BY order_quarter, customer_country
```

Front matter: `dimensions: [_calendar.quarter_label, customer.based_in_country]`, `measure: ORDER.FREIGHT_ORDERS_AMOUNT`, `aggregation: sum`, `time_grain: quarter`.

## 5. `docs/questions/02-…/staged.sql` — the control

Two `__current` views and a `LEFT JOIN`, which is where ADR 0005's "the control query has a shelf life" bill starts arriving early: the control now has to make the same join decision the bridge does, and if it were written `INNER` the two queries would agree and both be wrong.

```sql
-- The control. Straight from what the source sent, bypassing the business model and the
-- star schema. It may not mention dab or dar__uss: independence is the whole value.
SELECT
    strftime(o.order_date, '%Y') || '-Q' || cast(quarter(o.order_date) AS VARCHAR) AS order_quarter,
    c.country AS customer_country,
    cast(sum(o.freight) AS DECIMAL(28, 8)) AS freight_orders_amount
FROM das__staged.orders__current AS o
LEFT JOIN das__staged.customers__current AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE o.order_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY strftime(o.order_date, '%Y') || '-Q' || cast(quarter(o.order_date) AS VARCHAR), c.country
ORDER BY order_quarter, customer_country
```

Expected on the recording: 153 rows, grand total 64942.69, first row `('1996-Q3', 'Austria', 286.57)`.

## 6. `checks/` — the three generated checks

```sql
-- checks/order__placed__conservation.sql
-- Generated from dab/uss.yaml. Do not edit; regenerate.
SELECT
    (
        SELECT count(DISTINCT e."ORDER_key")
        FROM dab."view_ORDER_hist" AS e
        WHERE e."PLACED_ON" IS NOT NULL
    ) - (
        SELECT count(*)
        FROM dar__uss._bridge AS b
        WHERE b._stage = 'order' AND b._event = 'placed'
    ) AS disagreements;
```

```sql
-- checks/order_is_placed_by_customer__one_target.sql
-- Generated from dab/model.yaml. Do not edit; edit the model.
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT
        pair."ORDER_key" AS source_key,
        pair."CUSTOMER_key" AS target_key
    FROM dab."v_ORDER_IS_PLACED_BY_CUSTOMER" AS pair
    WHERE pair.rel_name = 'ORDER_IS_PLACED_BY_CUSTOMER'
    QUALIFY rank() OVER (
        PARTITION BY pair."ORDER_key"
        ORDER BY pair.eff_tmstp DESC, pair.ver_tmstp DESC
    ) = 1
)

SELECT count(*) - count(DISTINCT latest.source_key) AS ambiguities
FROM latest;
```

```sql
-- checks/order_is_placed_by_customer__no_strangers.sql
-- Generated from dab/model.yaml. Do not edit; edit the model.
SELECT count(*) AS strangers
FROM dar__uss._bridge AS b
LEFT JOIN dab."v_ORDER_IS_PLACED_BY_CUSTOMER" AS pair
    ON b.order_key = pair."ORDER_key" AND b.customer_key = pair."CUSTOMER_key"
WHERE
    b._stage = 'order'
    AND b.customer_key IS NOT NULL
    AND pair."ORDER_key" IS NULL;
```

## 7. The machinery change, stated as a diff of intent

`entity_keys()` currently reads `touched = {event.entity_id for event in uss.events}`. It becomes `touched | reached`, where `reached` is the set of target entities of every relationship whose source is touched — one hop. `_generate()` builds a peripheral for the same set, not for `uss.events`. `_stage_cte()` emits one `pair__<relationship_id>` CTE per walked edge and one `LEFT JOIN` per edge. `_branch()`'s key rule becomes: the stage's own key, an inherited key from the walk, or `cast(NULL AS VARCHAR)`. A relationship whose target is itself the source of another relationship raises `UssError` naming slice 5.
evidence: `daana-cli lint model-card.yaml` (relationship with `cardinality: MANY_TO_ONE`), exit 1: "✘ Errors:  Invalid Relationship Field: Relationships only support name, definition, description, source and target fields  • Invalid field 'cardinality' in relationship 'BELONGS_TO'. Valid fields are: name, definition, description, source, target, source_entity_id, target_entity_id, type". That list is the whole grammar.

The one candidate field is unvalidated. `daana-cli lint` over six variants of `type:` on the same relationship: `type=BANANA -> exit=0`, `type=MANY_TO_ONE -> exit=0`, `type=N:1 -> exit=0`, `type=1:1 -> exit=0`, `type=M:N -> exit=0`, `type=42 -> exit=0`, all with no output at all.

And it is dropped on compile. I added `type: "MANY_TO_ONE"` to an isolated copy of the probe model and ran `daana-cli deploy --no-tui` (exit 0). The regenerated `model.json` relationship is `{"source_entity_id": "CHILD", "target_entity_id": "PARENT", "name": "BELONGS_TO", "definition": …, "description": …, "atomic_context": "CHILD_BELONGS_TO_PARENT"}` and `'MANY_TO_ONE' in open('model.json').read()` is `False`. The generated `f_CHILD_PARENT_x` macro after that deploy is byte-identical to the one before it.

The vendor's own two artefacts disagree on direction. `daana-cli` model template: `relationships: - name: PLACES … source_entity_id: CUSTOMER_ENTITY  # Entity that 'owns' the relationship / target_entity_id: ORDER_ENTITY` — the one-to-many direction. The daana tutorial (blog/doc-ch1.txt:174): `- name: IS_PLACED_BY … source_entity_id: ORDER / target_entity_id: CUSTOMER` — the many-to-one direction.

The three readable pair objects, from a real deployed DuckDB warehouse. Base table `dab."CHILD_PARENT_x"`: `CHILD_key, PARENT_key, type_key, eff_tmstp, ver_tmstp, row_st, data_key, inst_key, inst_row_key, popln_tmstp` — 7 rows for 6 children, because CH1 and CH5 each have two. Internal view: `CREATE VIEW dab.v_CHILD_BELONGS_TO_PARENT AS SELECT an.CHILD_key, an.PARENT_key, bn.val_str AS rel_name, an.eff_tmstp, an.ver_tmstp, an.row_st, … FROM dab.CHILD_PARENT_x AS an INNER JOIN dab__meta.atom_contx_desc AS bn ON ((an.type_key = CAST(bn.atom_contx_key AS BIGINT)))` — no ranking, no relationship filter, so the `rel_name` predicate is not decoration. Presentation macro: `SELECT CHILD_key, PARENT_key, type_key, eff_tmstp, ver_tmstp FROM (SELECT …, rank() OVER (PARTITION BY CHILD_key, type_key ORDER BY eff_tmstp DESC, ver_tmstp DESC) AS nbr FROM dab.CHILD_PARENT_x WHERE (eff_tmstp <= CAST(p_eff_tmstp AS TIMESTAMP))) AS A WHERE ((nbr = 1) AND (row_st = 'Y'))` — `rank()`, not `row_number()`.

The four reads, run against that warehouse over a stage whose truth is 6 rows and 210.75. `A truth (stage only): [(6, Decimal('210.75000000'))]`; `B INNER JOIN raw pair table: [(7, Decimal('211.25000000'))]`; `B2 LEFT JOIN raw pair table: [(8, Decimal('271.25000000'))]`; `C INNER JOIN relationship view: [(6, Decimal('200.75000000'))]`; `C2 LEFT JOIN relationship view: [(7, Decimal('260.75000000'))]`; `D LEFT JOIN deduped v_ (proposal) rows,total,nonnullkeys: [(6, Decimal('210.75000000'), 5)]`. C is the dangerous one: right row count, wrong money.
